q: What shape is a boxing ring?
note: Early prize fights were held in a circle of spectators, and the name stuck even after the roped square replaced it.

q: Tennis has four Grand Slam tournaments: the Australian Open, the French Open, Wimbledon and which other?
note: It is the only one of the four played on hard courts under floodlights in New York each September.

q: In chess, how many pawns does each player have at the start of a game?
note: They fill the whole second row, one in front of each of the eight bigger pieces.

q: In blackjack, what total are players trying to reach without going over?
note: Going over is called busting, and it loses the hand immediately no matter what the dealer holds.

q: In poker, what is the name of the highest possible hand, made up of ten, jack, queen, king and ace all in the same suit?
note: It is simply the top end of a straight flush, which is why no separate rule is needed to rank it first.

q: In ten-pin bowling, what is it called when a player knocks down all ten pins using two balls in the same frame?
note: A spare is marked on the scoresheet with a slash, while a strike gets an X.

q: How many metres long is the swimming pool used for Olympic competition?
note: Races in a 25-metre pool are called short course and are listed in separate record books.

q: In soccer, what kick is awarded to the attacking team when a defender puts the ball out of play over his own goal line?
note: The ball is placed in the quarter-circle arc at whichever corner flag it went out nearest.

q: How many metres is one lap of a standard outdoor running track, measured in the inside lane?
note: Because the outer lanes are longer, sprint races up to 400 metres use staggered starting positions.

q: Sailing's America's Cup is not named after the United States. What is it named after?
note: The schooner America won a race round the Isle of Wight in 1851, and the trophy it carried home took the boat's name.

q: The word soccer began as a British abbreviation of which two-word name for the game?
note: Oxford students clipped assoc to soc and added -er, the same slang habit that gave rugby the nickname rugger.

q: Cricket's Ashes series got its name from a mock obituary for English cricket, printed after England lost at home in 1882 to which country?
note: The spoof notice said English cricket had died and the body would be cremated, which is why the prize is a small urn.

q: The name of which martial art translates from Japanese as empty hand?
note: It developed on Okinawa, and the empty-hand name marks it out from the island's weapon-based fighting styles.

q: Which stick-and-ball team sport, long played by Indigenous peoples of North America, takes its name from the French for the stick?
note: French missionaries wrote of the game as la crosse, after the crook-shaped stick it is played with.

q: Table tennis is widely known by which other name, which started life as a trademarked brand?
note: Because the name was owned by games manufacturers, clubs and federations adopted the neutral title table tennis instead.

q: Which Italian cycling race puts its overall leader in a pink jersey?
note: The pink matches the paper of the sponsoring sports newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport.

q: In rugby league, how many players from each team are on the field?
note: The thirteen-a-side game is the main point of difference from rugby union, which fields two more players per team.

q: In cricket, what are the two small pieces of wood balanced on top of the stumps called?
note: A batter is bowled only when the delivery knocks a bail clean out of its groove.

q: What is the highest break a player can make in a standard frame of snooker?
note: It takes all fifteen reds, each followed by the black, and then the six colours in order.

q: In professional darts, what score does each player start a leg on?
note: The odd extra point forces players to finish on a double, since 500 could be checked out with plain scoring.

q: What is the name of the chess move in which the king and one of the rooks both move at the same time?
note: It is the only move in chess that shifts two of your own pieces in one turn.

q: Apart from the Q, which letter tile is worth ten points in English-language Scrabble?
note: The point values were set by counting letter frequencies in newspaper pages, which is why the rarest letters score most.

q: In the high jump, what is the name of the technique in which the athlete clears the bar head-first and on their back?
note: Dick Fosbury won Olympic gold with it in 1968, and within a decade almost every jumper had copied him.

q: In basketball, what is the violation called when a player moves their feet illegally while holding the ball instead of dribbling?
note: The penalty is simply a turnover, with the other side given the ball from the sideline.

q: The sport of badminton is named after Badminton House, the English country seat of which duke?
note: The game was popularised by guests at the house in the 1860s and carried its address as its name.

q: The French Open is also called Roland-Garros, after a Frenchman famous for what, rather than for tennis?
note: Roland Garros made the first flight across the Mediterranean in 1913 and the Paris stadium was named in his memory.

q: The original soccer World Cup trophy, stolen in Brazil in 1983 and never recovered, was named after which FIFA president?
note: Brazil had been allowed to keep it permanently after a third World Cup win in 1970, and a new trophy has been used since 1974.

q: Monopoly grew out of an earlier board game patented in 1904 by Elizabeth Magie. What was that game called?
note: Magie designed it to argue against land monopolies, so the game was meant as a warning rather than a celebration.

q: The name of which Olympic sport comes from a Greek word meaning naked?
note: Greek athletes trained unclothed in a building called the gymnasion, which is also where the word gymnasium comes from.

q: In sumo wrestling, what is the name of the raised clay circle in which bouts take place?
note: Its edge is marked by half-buried bales of rice straw, and stepping outside them loses the bout.
